utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Now, before the boxes were transported, were those boxes sealed?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT
utterances.text: I believe so, that the boxes were sealed. But the proper procedure of sealing the material was carried out later in the base. However, let me point out that at no point the boxes were out of my sight or out of my reach. I mean, I was the custodian. And if I had to leave the boxes even for a minute, I would make sure that an OTP staff, especially an investigator, is present at the site where the boxes are.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Now, they were taken to the base from which you were working and properly sealed there. What was actually done?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT
utterances.text: Once again, at the -- at the base, what we did was we checked the evidence register forms to make sure that everything we had seized was in the boxes. So the custodians then went through the material once again. Once that had been done, the cardboard boxes were sealed with adhesive tape, I guess, and then it was secured from all sides so that it cannot be tampered with during its shipping to The Hague Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And from the base in which you were operating, were the boxes taken to the offices of the UN, the Office of the Prosecutor in Zagreb?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT
utterances.text: Yes. Once we had completed the packing of the boxes, the boxes then were handed over to one specific investigator of the Office of the Prosecutor who had gone with us on this mission, and he transported the material to the Zagreb field office, where they were put into diplomatic pouches.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And from there, were they sent to the Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT
utterances.text: From there, the same investigator who transported the material to the Zagreb field office then accompanied the material with the Tribunal's driver and a UN vehicle provided by the Zagreb field office all the way to The Hague.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. And thereafter, I think it was dealt with by other members of the staff employed here.

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Thank you. So that was the first search in Prijedor in December 1997. Was the second search in Banja Luka?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT
utterances.text: The second search was conducted in Banja Luka.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And was that on the 27th of February of 1998?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I'm going to ask again -- obviously, these ones don't work on the board -- if plans of Banja Luka could be handed out, and again one placed on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Just before we deal with that, Mr. Inayat, I've got to ask you one matter. When you were conducting the search in Prijedor in 1997, were you assisted by any outside agency other than the Office of the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT
utterances.text: That is correct, that the Office of the Prosecutor was assisted by other organisations, such as the SFOR and the IPTF.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And their role being what?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT
utterances.text: In 1997, the situation in Prijedor was still volatile, and I remember that in 1996, even some of our staff members were going to be arrested by the local police there. So there seemed to be some threat that we would not be able to carry out our work without SFOR support. So a request was put in, and the SFOR and IPTF accompanied us to all these positions. And their support was merely to ensure that we are given the protection, and in case of any untoward incident, we are evacuated immediately from the area. That was the only support that they gave us.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: So they didn't actually take part in the searches themselves?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT
utterances.text: That was all in black and white made very clear to us and to the SFOR that that assistance was not being sought, and they did not provide us with any such assistance.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Now, Banja Luka, in February 1998, again had a search warrant been issued by this Tribunal enabling you to carry out searches at five locations?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT
utterances.text: That is correct that on 13th of February a search warrant was issued again and signed by Judge Fouad Riad. And pursuant to that search warrant, these five locations were searched in Banja Luka city.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Can you tell Their Honours which were the five locations that were searched?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And point them out at the same time.

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT
utterances.text: For orientation purposes, I'd just like to point out that this is the north of Banja Luka city. Bosanska Gradiska is to the north. And we have Celinac here to the east and Kotor Varos and Sipovo to the south-east, Milana Vrhovica to the south and Prijedor to the west. This, Your Honours -- this, Your Honours, this road that I am indicating is the Mladen Stojanovic -- I ask for forgiveness if my pronunciation is not correct. But this is the Mladen Stojanovic street. And at this point, this street is renamed into Kralj Petar Karadjordjevic. It is in fact at this location where the municipal building, which I'll mark now, and the presidential palace or what is also known as Banski Dvor are located. And I also believe that this road before the war was probably also known as Marshal Tito Street. And this, Your Honours, this red area - I'm going to draw a circle - is the CSB building.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Well, first of all, you searched the municipal building, did you?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT
utterances.text: I personally went to the municipal building, but the searches at all locations were conducted simultaneously.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. So -- sorry, not you personally. A search was conducted at the municipal building.

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And the presidential palace?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT
utterances.text: That is correct. Because the presidential palace housed the offices of the SDS on the ground floor, they had two rooms. And on the first and second floor of the presidential palace were the offices of SRT, the Serbian Radio and Television located. Although the television studios and administration building was in the presidential palace, but the radio station -- the physical premises of the radio station were located outside on Kralj Petar Karadjordjevic, very close to the centre.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. So --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the counsel and witness please be asked to slow down and to make pauses between answer and question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. You heard the message.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Sir, just to make sure that we're all following this, the municipal building was searched?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT
utterances.text: Yes, the municipal building was searched.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: The presidential palace, because it contained SDS offices and offices of Serbian Radio and Television.

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT
utterances.text: They were also searched.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And the next circle that you drew.

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Was for the -- which building?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT
utterances.text: CSB building.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: That being the police --

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT
utterances.text: The police station, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Is that the regional --

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT
utterances.text: That is the regional.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And any other buildings?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT
utterances.text: Your Honours, this road that I'm pointing out is the road called Aleja Svetog Save, and it runs right here where the 1st Krajina Corps headquarters are located. It's a massive eight-storey building. And I'll draw a circle. This is where the 1st Krajina Corps headquarters were. This was another building that was searched on that same day.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Any other buildings that day?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT
utterances.text: I did point out that the radio station, although we pointed out, was in the presidential palace. But actually we found out later that it is not, so we searched that building also, which is on Karadjordjevic, which I've just pointed out.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Okay. Again --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honours, that should then be marked, please, Prosecution Exhibit number 2.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: P2. That will be number P2.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I think again, Mr. Inayat, the investigation was conducted by a large team of investigators, lawyers, analysts, and language staff.

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And were you, as you've told us, involved personally in the search of the municipal building?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT
utterances.text: I was personally involved, but I was also the custodian of the evidence that was seized. And later in the evening for a very brief time, I also went to the 1st Krajina Corps headquarters to assist the investigation team there.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I think in fact the search of the 1st Krajina Corps headquarters went over into the next day, whereas the search of the other buildings was completed in one day.

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT
utterances.text: That is correct. The search of the Krajina Corps headquarters concluded on 28th, around about 10.00 in the morning.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And were the same procedures followed in respect of how the documents were dealt with, as you described to us in respect of Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT
utterances.text: This time around, I would believe that even more care was taken when filling out information on the evidence register forms to try to give as much information as possible. So if anything, we were being more cautious of seizing evidence and trying to register as much detail as possible.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: But again, eventually was the material taken to Zagreb and from there to The Hague?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT
utterances.text: Yes, it was. And if I -- although I was not asked, but I'd just like to point out that the evidence seized from the 1st Krajina Corps headquarters consisted of almost 35.000 pages. The evidence seized from the municipal building and the police headquarters, regional police headquarters, was almost 145.000 pages of documents. And of course, from SRTV, the Serbian Radio and Television, we also seized reel-to-reel tapes and some transcripts of announcements that were made, and yes, all this material was transported after properly being bagged in cardboard offices to the Zagreb field office.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Korner, when it's convenient for you TO pause a little bit, I would like to ask something out of the witness, but I don't want to interrupt the flow of questions.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, certainly not. I've finished that particular seizure so ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thought so. Mr. Inayat, I would like you now to mark with your own handwriting the place names that you have circled. In other words, in each of these maps where you have put those circles, please indicate what those circles are supposed to represent.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honours, you want me also to write the names?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. For example, in this last map that we are dealing with, the Banja Luka one, you circled four places, et cetera, because, later on, since this is being -- this is becoming an exhibit, one would not be in a position to know which circle -- what each circle represents what, unless you mark it now.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honours, the first --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Just write it on the document itself. That's what is being required of you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. The first circle where I'm pointing is, Your Honours, the CSP building, or the regional police headquarters. I have to admit my handwriting is not that good. Your Honours, the second circle I'm pointing at is the municipal building. "MB" for municipal building. Your Honours, the third circle I'm pointing to is the presidential palace, also known as Banski Dvor, so maybe I'll just put "Banski Dvor." Your Honours, the fourth circle I'm pointing to is the 1st Krajina Corps headquarters.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And you said that the TV station, in actual fact, was not located inside the BD, the presidential palace, but it was located elsewhere?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honours, the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You mentioned the street.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. The television station was located on the first and second floors of the presidential palace. However, the radio station was located outside, very close to these two circles that I've drawn, which is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Will you point that out?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, I can generally make a line here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Okay.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Very close to the municipal building and the president palace, and I can give you the address. It is Kralj Petar Karadjordjevic 127 and 129. This is the street address of the radio station.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Will you just put "RS," meaning radio station, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thanks. Are you happy with that? Ms. Korner?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you very much, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I would like you to do the same with the previous document. And I would like you to do the same with the first document, P1, the Prijedor one.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, it may be as well if Mr. Inayat were to initial and sign the document that he's -- so we know, in case a map has to be produced again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Go ahead. Do the same procedure, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honours, Your Honours, this circle that I'm pointing out is the SDS offices, so I will write "SDS." Your Honours, in fact, I should have drawn two circles here, but I've drawn one circle around both the police station and the municipal building, which in fact are within a hundred metres of each other. So if you want, I can just say municipal building and police station.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: So this, Your Honours, is the municipal building and the police station. Your Honours, the third circle that I am indicating is where the radio station Prijedor and the Kozarski Vjesnik offices were located. Radio station and Kozarski Vjesnik.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So suggest to you now to initial -- put your initials against those entries so that --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On the map?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: No, no. It's where you have -- where you have actually entered a circle and a --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, may I suggest that he just signs - because we can always get another copy of the map - if he just signs that -- one place on that map to show those are his --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Will that be acceptable with you?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JANU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. You can just sign and that should be okay. Both documents, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Again, Mr. Inayat, were you accompanied on this particular search by other agencies?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT
utterances.text: Again, the same procedures were adopted. SFOR and IPTF accompanied us to all these locations, and their primary purpose was to give us protection and not to search alongside with us.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Then the third seizure, was that again at Prijedor, conducted between the 27th and the 29th of October, 2000?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: On this occasion -- I'm sorry, again, on this occasion, was there -- were there searches conducted at six locations?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And could you just tell Their Honours which locations?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT
utterances.text: Your Honours, we went to the police station once again in Prijedor, and we also went to the police station in Omarska, which you will not be able to see on this city map, which is almost like 15 to 20 kilometres east of Prijedor, in the direction of Banja Luka. We also visited and searched the Omarska Iron Ore Mines, where the detention centre was operating in the summer of 1992. The fourth location, we went to the medical centre in Prijedor city, a place which we can see on this map. And the fifth place we went to was the health centre, which is different from the medical centre, in a separate building. And the sixth place we went to was the Ljubija Iron Ore Mines offices, because the Omarska Iron Ore Mines was supervised by the Ljubija Iron Ore Mines, so we went to their offices in Prijedor city. So these were the six sites we went to.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And I think, in effect, these searches were carried out relating to matters that had arisen in the trial of those charged with the camp at Omarska, Kvocka and others?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And on this occasion, I think they were conducted by means of what's called a Prosecutor's Summons for Assistance, as opposed to a search warrant?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT
utterances.text: I think the Prosecutor's Directive, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Directive, right. And again, I think documents were recovered. How were they dealt with on this occasion? In the same way as on the previous occasions?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT
utterances.text: This time, we had the advantage of three days at our disposal, and we were really very focused on what we were going to be seizing, and after a three-day search of these locations, we were able to gather about 2300 pages of documents from these six locations.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And how were they dealt with?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT
utterances.text: Because the collection was very small in comparison, the investigators who actually seized the material filled out the evidence register forms and brought this material with them to the Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: So on this occasion, one is able to identify which investigator found a particular document and where?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT
utterances.text: Exactly.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, I want to move, then, from the seizures of major document collections to other sources of documentation, and I think you have listed in your -- the annex to your statement, the various sources - and indeed, in your statement - the various sources of information. And if we can -- sorry, the various sources of supply of evidence. First of all, if we can deal with --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And Your Honours, I am looking now at the annex, and I propose to go through that because I think it's simpler.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: In the index to documents, you have identified the short form that you've used, the numbers, A-1, A-2 and so forth. The first category, you say Evidence Submitted by the Embassy of Bosnia and Herzegovina, The Hague, in the Netherlands. How is that evidence provided?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT
utterances.text: The BiH government appointed a liaison officer to the Tribunal in early 1995, and that person has been first using the premises in the Bosnian embassy in Brussels and then later moved to The Hague. So the liaison officer who sits in the Bosnian embassy receives requests from us to get the documents and occasionally, when he comes to the Tribunal, he hands over the material here.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And on occasions, is material supplied without a request, that they think may be of interest to the Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT
utterances.text: That has happened also.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Then could we move to the next category, your A-2, the Minister of -- the Ministry of the Interior in Sarajevo, Bosnia-Herzegovina? How is that material acquired?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT
utterances.text: Maybe I need to just give a little bit of a background here, that in May of 1992, when the Serbian government moved its headquarters to Pale from Sarajevo, many offices that were left with a lot of material were reviewed by the Ministry of Interior and they were seized and brought to the Ministry of Interior. And in late 1994, we were informed about this collection. In February of 1995, members of the Office of the Prosecutor reviewed that material in the Ministry of Interior, which consisted of over 100.000 pages and documents -- 23.000 pages were identified and they were recovered from the Ministry of Interior, first by scanning but in later years they even gave us the hard copies.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Next category, 2nd Military District, Sarajevo. How did those documents come into our possession?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT
utterances.text: There is a very little collection of these documents that are mentioned in the exhibit list, and these documents also came to us from the headquarters of the 2nd Military District, where they were reviewed and taken into possession.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: The CSB Sarajevo, that being the Security Services Centre?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT
utterances.text: Yes. Again, there have been many missions by the Office of the Prosecutor staff to this building, where documents have been made available to us and we have taken possession of those documents.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Then next, AID in Sarajevo, and you've explained that stands -- the initials stand for the Agency for Investigation and Documentation?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT
utterances.text: Since January of 1996, when this agency was created, since that point, our main sources of documents have come from them in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Then we can see that the State Security Service in Bihac has provided documents?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT
utterances.text: Yes. If you want, I can give some background here also, that --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Mr. Inayat, I think if anybody wants to ask you further questions, they can. We are just establishing --

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT
utterances.text: Yes. SDB Bihac has also provided us with a lot of material.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Then we see the same agency AID in Bihac, in Sanski Most, in Bugojno and in Tesanj have also provided documents?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT
utterances.text: Yes. And let me point out that SDB Bihac became AID Bihac in 1996.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: So that's -- the A-6 and A-7 category relate to the same organisation?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Then we -- the Office of the Prosecutor has received --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, I note the time. I don't think I can unfortunately finish this list today if, as Your Honours said, we have to adjourn so the next case can come in. So it may be an appropriate --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] Madam Registrar, is the other Trial Chamber --

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: I'm checking on that. Your Honour, this afternoon, Courtroom I will be available. There is no second trial this afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Can we go on for another 15 minutes? Madam Fauveau?

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honours, the interpreters?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Ah, yes, the interpreters.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Who have been going now for an hour and a half.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That would leave us no option. Can we go on for another 15 minutes?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: We can manage, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I very much appreciate that. Thank you. So we go on for another 15 minutes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Then can we move to the next category, the Police Administration in the Municipality of Kljuc, "police administration" meaning what, Mr. Inayat?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT
utterances.text: Because Kljuc does not have an AID office, the section in the police station which deals with material that has to be handed to us is called the Police Administration.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: The 5th Corps headquarters in Bihac, that being the 5th Corps headquarters of the Bosnia-Herzegovina army?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: The Basic Court in Sanski Most, that speaks for itself. Then the next category are those covered -- I'm sorry, recovered during the search and seizure operation in Banja Luka?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And B-2 is -- specifically relates to the documents that were seized from the 1st Krajina Corps headquarters?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Next we have some documents supplied by Croatian authorities and television archives in Zagreb, who provided, I think, video; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct, yeah.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Then the next category that is on the list is evidence of the exhumations -- or from the exhumations which were carried out by the Office of the Prosecutor in this Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Then the next category, evidence recovered as a result of exhumations conducted by the Bosnian State Commission for Missing Persons?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: "M" is the catch-all one, miscellaneous, but I think, if required, you can deal with where the miscellaneous come from?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT
utterances.text: Well, basically any documents that are not from any of these other legends are given the word "miscellaneous" for it.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: The next category is self-evident, open-source material. In that, you include, do you, newspaper articles, books and the like?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Anything that is available to the public at large?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: The next category, P-1, relates to evidence recovered as a result of the seizure operation in Prijedor on the 12th of December, 1997, and the category after that, the second search in Prijedor in October, 2000?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Then we come to documents obtained from the Republika Srpska liaison officer to the ICTY. Perhaps you could just give us a little detail about how this works?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT
utterances.text: The liaison officer for the Republika Srpska was appointed in June, 1996, and since then we have had three liaison officers, and they occasionally visit the Tribunal. The Office of the Prosecutor submits a request for assistance and which are then taken back by the liaison officer to Republika Srpska and served on relevant departments from whom the material is being requested. In a few cases, we have received documents from the liaison officer of the Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I think it can be summarised in this way: That in some cases, requests have resulted in documents; in other cases, they have not?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT
utterances.text: I would say in the majority of the cases we have not received documents.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And then the second category, R-2, I don't think we need go through the names but a number of officials in the Republika Srpska who, in one form or another, have provided documents?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Then I think there are a very few where documentation does not reveal what the source of the documents is?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT
utterances.text: I'd like to add here that when I prepared this list, there were a couple of documents where I could not find any information on the sources. However, since then, I have located the sources. And there is one particular document that, if you want, I can point out, we know the source. So really, there might still be just one document where the source is unknown, which, if we make more efforts, hopefully we can find the source there also.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And I think the last two categories are obvious again, transcripts and judgements of the Courts here and the witnesses themselves who have supplied documents?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes. Your Honours, I now intend to turn to the particular documents which are the subject of dispute, so I don't know whether Your Honours wish me to start now. I know we've been given --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Well, I think considering our decision, the response that was forthcoming from the Defence teams, I think it makes more sense to stop now so that you can go through this whole list and identify them with more precision and limit yourself to those. I think it will be easier.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You have already?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes. As I say, we were supplied, as a result of Your Honour's order, with the actual documents, at least I think. It was sometimes difficult to work out because Madam Fauveau gave us the documents they disputed, Mr. Ackerman let us know which ones he didn't dispute. So it was occasionally complicated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: If you can proceed then for the next ten minutes, we can go ahead and -- provided that after ten minutes we stop.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes. Your Honours, before I do that, may I deal -- in case I forget, there is an application which I should have made earlier, but the first is Mr. Inayat clearly won't be finished giving evidence today. He's still in chief. He's my lead investigator. I would again like permission to speak to him after the Court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I wouldn't imagine -- okay, permission granted.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I'm grateful. The other - and I was reminded of this - is that under Rule 90(D) of the Rules - and perhaps I can read it to Your Honour: "Notwithstanding paragraph (C)" - that's witnesses shall not be present when other witnesses testify - "upon order of the Chamber, an investigator in charge of a party's investigation shall not be precluded from being called as a witness on the ground that he or she has been present in the courtroom during the proceedings." Now, although Mr. Inayat hasn't in fact been present, he will clearly from what's happened today be coming and going. There are facilities for him to watch the proceedings. As Your Honour may know, there are cameras. And effectively, although he isn't present, he will be from time to time watching, and I'd like Your Honour's permission for that. The reason is quite simply this: If something arises on which I need to have an investigator investigate immediately, it takes much longer if the investigator knows nothing about it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Ackerman.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, this matter has become kind of -- I don't know what word I'm looking for. But now that we're broadcasting the proceedings on the Internet so that anybody in the world can watch what's going on, I don't think it makes much difference. The witnesses who are coming here can sit in their homes and watch our proceedings, and if they want to, they will know what everybody has testified before got here, which is what we were trying to prevent, but now we can't do that anymore, so I don't care what you do with it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Ms. Fauveau.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have no objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Permission granted, in any case.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And Your Honour, can I invite Your Honours to turn to the binders that relate to Dr. Donia. Your Honours, I understand that the first document that is objected to Your Honours will find behind divider 3, headed "Excerpts from the Minutes of the Sixth Session of the Bosanska Krajina Community of Municipalities."

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And that document, Mr. Inayat, I think bears the Serbo-Croat version as the numbers 00403850251. Can you tell Your Honours where that was obtained from?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT
utterances.text: This document was given to one of our investigators who has left this Tribunal now, Mr. Grant MacIntosh, on 25th of April, 1996, by Mr. Boro Blagojevic who was the former secretary of the ARK assembly. That was given, as I said, on the 25th of April in 1996 in Banja Luka in the municipal building.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: As you point out, he was the secretary to the regional assembly of the Autonomous Region?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT
utterances.text: And also the Crisis Staff.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Then if we move to the next document, which Your Honours, as I understand it -- and this is why I say I'm quite confused about the criteria that's being applied. It's behind divider 7. It appears to be a signed, stamped document, bearing the number -- I'm not sure what's happened to the translation here. It may be one of the ones -- yes, I think it's one of the ones, if you'll recall, there was no translation.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: But the number, Mr. Inayat, is 00403790.

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Can you tell us --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] Yes, Mr. Ackerman.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: The objection is that there's no translation. I can't figure out what the document says. And it may be that once there's a translation, I won't have an objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But in any case, let the witness give us the information as to the source. That's not going to change depending on the translation. And we will visit that later. Yes, Mr. Inayat.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours, the document 00403790 was once again given on the 25th of April, 1996 in the Banja Luka municipal building to our investigator Mr. Grant MacIntosh by the former secretary of the Crisis Staff and the assembly, Mr. Boro Blagojevic.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Mike, please. Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Microphone again, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: The next document is the one following after divider 8, "Minutes of the Second Session of the Assembly, the Community of Municipalities." The Serbo-Croat version beginning at 004 -- I'm sorry, the number beginning at 00403806.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Mr. Inayat, where do the records show that came from?

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT
utterances.text: I'm trying to find this ERN number on this list. Did you say 00403806?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MAZHAR INAYAT
utterances.text: This document was also given by Mr. Boro Blagojevic on the same date, that is, 26th of April, 1996, to Mr. Grant MacIntosh in the municipal building of Banja Luka.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honours, would that then be a convenient --.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Ackerman.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I think we are developing a record problem with regard to these documents, Judge. What we're doing is we're creating a record of where they came from and something that -- you know, some of the basis upon which the Court can make a decision as to the reliability and so forth by reference to numbers that are going to disappear. At some point, these are going to be called "P" something or other. And I don't know how in the world we can cross-reference back in the transcript from a document that is admitted as P10 to a discussion we had about the document behind tab 8, because it's just going to be lost in the transcript. You'll try to search -- if you search for Exhibit P7, you'll find --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I agree it may create problems. But obviously here we have a binder with -- a folder with I don't know how many documents. The options are very simple: We can either have them exhibited now en bloc and the Trial Chamber will admit them en bloc obviously without prejudice to what -- all the caveats that we mentioned earlier, and they will be numbered, and then we can take it up. We have only covered three documents, in any case, and therefore the problem is not that serious for the moment. I appreciate your remark, because actually it was something which I had on my mind. I didn't quite know how we are going -- we were going to go through this. But I think your suggestion and my suggestion will make things easier.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm happy with that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So if you can therefore please ask for these documents, this folder, to be exhibited.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I do. I formally ask that these documents be exhibited with the following numbers --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, exactly. And these documents are being admitted in evidence and will be marked by the registry as P3 and or "P" whatever. And then do it in whichever way you do it usually. And we'll take it up from there tomorrow morning, and there will be more specific reference then to the various documents. Mr. Inayat, you will come here again tomorrow morning, please, at 9.00 sharp.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And the Prosecutor will continue with her examination-in-chief. Thank you. In the meantime, there is a dispensation from the usual restriction, and she can consult with you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm grateful. Can I also say that we've also handed to Your Honour's legal officer a draft of the summons that we'd ask Your Honour to issue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I will deal with that today. That's for the journalist, you mean?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: That's for the journalist.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And if I could just remind Your Honour if we could have a decision on the Rule 92 witnesses.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We'll try to work on that.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you. I thank the interpreters for their patience. It's very much appreciated. We'll resume our work tomorrow morning at 9.00 sharp. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: at 2.02 p.m., to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 29th day of January, 2002, at 9.00 a.m.
